messages.text:
I propose narrowing the draft’s subcontractor, retention, and publicity permissions as follows:

**Access and subcontracting.** Access would be limited to named archive personnel and studio scanning/QC staff. For the first batch only, I would use an external color specialist, identified for the archive’s written approval before access. The specialist would be bound by equivalent confidentiality terms, with no onward subcontracting, and would use an individual, logged account in the studio’s encrypted workspace. Source files would remain read-only; no local downloads or personal devices would be permitted.

For accurate calibration, I prefer that the specialist have temporary access to the first-batch **master images**, solely for color and tonal calibration. Masters preserve the full capture context and reduce the risk of a second calibration pass. Access would end when calibration is complete, and no later than the ten-day correction window. If master-image access is not acceptable, the alternative is to supply the color-target frames and archive-approved, content-minimized extracts, with any resulting recalibration treated as a follow-up technical review rather than broader access.

**QC, correction, and deletion.** For each batch, the studio would retain active working files for **ten calendar days after delivery** for archive QC and scan corrections. If corrections are requested within that window, only the affected files would be retained until the corrections are accepted, for up to ten further calendar days unless we agree an extension in writing.

Within **two business days after acceptance or expiry of the applicable correction window**, the studio would delete active working copies and revoke project access. The specialist’s copies, if any, would be deleted at calibration completion, with deletion confirmed to the archive. Encrypted studio backups would remain inaccessible for ordinary work, would not be used for further processing, and would age out under the existing **45-day rotation**. The schedule should distinguish these studio copies from any preservation masters retained by the archive itself.

**Publicity.** The studio would like to publish one anonymized process image, but anonymization alone would not authorize publication. We would submit the exact image and caption for prior written consent, with no legible letter text, donor identifiers, distinctive document features, or identifying metadata. Consent would be limited to the approved image and stated use; all other publicity would remain prohibited.

The principal tradeoff is therefore full-master access for a tightly controlled specialist versus a more restricted calibration workflow that may require additional review. Does the archive prefer that fallback, and are the ten-day active retention and 45-day backup cutoff acceptable?

**Access and calibration.** We propose the restricted workflow for the first batch and accept that it may require a second calibration pass. The archive will identify the two restricted collections before capture. Only named archive personnel may view handwriting or identifying content from those collections. We will segregate those materials and hold them back if scanning would expose that content to studio staff or the specialist.

For the other collections, named studio scanning and QC staff may handle the files. We will supply a calibration sheet. The external specialist may see only the resulting target frames and masked extracts from those other collections that the archive approves in writing. We accept your proposed confidentiality, account, logging and device controls. The archive must approve the specialist by name before access and each extract before release. A second pass may use further approved extracts under the same terms. Revoke the specialist’s access at calibration completion or ten calendar days after first-batch delivery, whichever comes first.

**Retention and deletion.** We accept ten calendar days from batch delivery for QC, ending sooner on written acceptance. A correction requested in that window extends retention only for affected files, until acceptance or ten further calendar days, whichever comes first. Any extension needs a written agreement identifying the files and a new deadline. Within two business days of each applicable cutoff, delete the studio’s active copies, including extracts and temporary files, and revoke access to that batch. Please send a dated deletion record identifying the batch, files covered, deletion date and access revocations. Confirm the specialist’s access closure and deletion of any workspace copies at calibration completion. Archive preservation masters remain with the archive.

The **45-day backup rotation is the outstanding retention exception**. Can you exclude pilot files from backups? If exclusion is infeasible, we could accept the rotation for the other collections if each backup copy expires within 45 calendar days of creation, restores reapply deletions before staff regain access, and you confirm final expiry in writing for each batch. Please confirm which arrangement you can support.

**Incidents.** Before signing, let’s enter a named incident lead, monitored email and urgent phone number for each party. The studio should notify the archive lead without delay and within 24 hours of learning of suspected loss, unauthorized access or disclosure. Give the affected batch and containment steps known at the time, then update us as the facts develop.

**Publicity.** We would consider one photograph of equipment alone. Keep collection materials, document images, identifying screens, labels and metadata out of the photograph. Submit the exact photograph, caption and intended publication channel for written archive approval before use. Signing the schedule grants no publicity consent.

The studio accepts the restricted calibration workflow, including prior written approval of the specialist and each extract, archive segregation of the two restricted collections, and specialist access ending at calibration completion or ten calendar days after first-batch delivery, whichever comes first. Any second pass will use only newly approved extracts under the same controls.

**Backups:** The studio cannot reliably exclude pilot files from its backup system. We therefore accept the archive’s fallback and will apply it to all studio-held pilot data, including approved target frames and extracts:

- Each encrypted backup copy will expire no later than **45 calendar days after its creation**.
- After active-copy deletion, no further backup of the deleted material will be created; existing backup copies will age out under that limit.
- The studio will maintain a deletion register. Any restored pilot data will remain quarantined until applicable deletions and access revocations have been reapplied; staff and specialist access will not resume beforehand.
- For each batch, the studio will confirm in writing the final backup expiry within **two business days after the last backup copy containing that batch expires**.

We also accept the active-copy deletion cutoffs and dated deletion records covering the batch, files or file ranges, deletion date, and access revocations. Specialist access closure and deletion of workspace copies will be confirmed at calibration completion.

**Incidents:** We accept notification without delay and in any event within 24 hours of learning of a suspected loss, unauthorized access, or disclosure, with the affected batch and known containment steps followed by developing updates. The studio’s named incident lead, monitored incident email, and urgent phone number will be entered in the execution copy alongside the archive’s details before signing.

**Publicity:** We will limit the request to one equipment-only photograph, excluding collection materials, document images, identifying screens, labels, and metadata. The exact photograph, caption, and intended publication channel will be submitted for prior written approval. Any material change or additional channel will require separate approval; signing the schedule grants no publicity consent.

We accept the 45-day backup exception on the terms you set out. It applies to all pilot data the studio is authorized to hold, including approved target frames and masked extracts. The archive will hold back any material from the two restricted collections that would expose handwriting or identifying content to studio staff or the specialist.

We agree to include the access, calibration, retention, deletion evidence, incident notification and publicity terms as settled. No substantive exception remains open. Before signing, each party will enter its incident lead’s name, monitored email and urgent phone number in the execution copy.

The first masked calibration test did not preserve an ink-tone distinction needed to verify capture fidelity. We therefore need one narrow amendment to the restricted workflow, without seeking general master-image access.

**Supervised verification review.** We propose that the approved specialist attend a single, supervised review at the archive using one archive-selected sample from a **nonrestricted** collection. Archive personnel and the studio QC lead would be present. The review would be limited to comparing that sample with its displayed master on calibrated equipment to verify the missing tonal distinction and determine whether recalibration or rescanning is required.

No restricted-collection material would be included. The specialist would receive no remote or broader file access, and no copies, downloads, photographs, or extracts would leave the review. Any notes would be limited to technical calibration observations. The review would end the specialist’s involvement unless the archive approves a further review in writing. This trades a brief, controlled content review for the verification risk created by masking, while leaving the remote-access restrictions intact.

**Rescan acceptance before deletion.** We also propose adding an operator acceptance test to the correction procedure. Before the working copy of a rescan is deleted, the assigned scanning operator must complete and record a test covering:

- completeness, focus, resolution, and geometry;
- color and tonal reproduction against the calibration target and source; and
- specifically, preservation of the ink-tone distinction that prompted the correction.

A failed test would require another rescan rather than acceptance. Only the affected working files would remain in the correction workflow. The test would be completed within the existing correction window, followed by archive acceptance where required and deletion within the agreed two-business-day period. If more time is needed, the existing requirement for a written, file-specific extension and new deadline would apply; there would be no automatic extension. The deletion record would reference the completed acceptance test.

All other access, backup-expiry, deletion-evidence, incident, and publicity terms remain unchanged. Can these two provisions be added to the execution copy?

We can add both provisions if the execution copy specifies the comparison sheet, who signs off on color, and what happens if verification fails.

**Supervised review.** We can make the nonrestricted comparison original available for one morning next week. With the archive conservator supervising and the studio QC lead present, the approved specialist may compare that sheet with its capture on a calibrated display at the archive. Only an archive-approved masked image of the sheet may leave the archive. The specialist may record technical observations only and may neither photograph the review nor retain an unmasked copy. No donor letter or donor-letter master may be shown or supplied to the specialist. The session ends the specialist’s involvement unless we approve a further review in writing.

**Color validation and scanning.** The specialist advises on calibration. The studio QC lead records whether the capture preserves the ink-tone distinction visible on the comparison original, and the archive conservator makes the final color determination. Test captures of the comparison sheet may proceed now. Production scanning that relies on this calibration may begin or resume only after the conservator confirms a pass in writing. If the distinction is lost, recalibrate and retest on the sheet before proceeding.

**Rescans and destruction.** The operator will record the proposed checks for completeness, focus, resolution, geometry, color and the specific ink-tone distinction. The QC lead will review the results and the conservator will confirm color before archive acceptance. A failed test calls for another rescan within the agreed window. Delete affected active working files within two business days of archive acceptance or expiry of the applicable correction window, whichever comes first. If the test is still failing or incomplete at expiry, record that status and delete on schedule unless both parties have already agreed in writing to a file-specific extension with a new deadline. Reference the test result or incomplete status in the deletion record. The agreed backup expiry and confirmation terms continue to apply.

Can the studio confirm these terms and the QC lead’s availability for the supervised morning?

The studio confirms both provisions. The studio QC lead is available for one supervised morning next week and will attend with the approved specialist once the archive confirms the date and start time.

The comparison sheet will be the archive-selected, nonrestricted original, identified in the test record. The review will take place under conservator supervision on a calibrated display at the archive. Only the archive-approved masked image may leave; the specialist will make technical observations only, take no photographs, retain no unmasked copy, and receive no donor letter or donor-letter master. That session ends the specialist’s involvement unless a further review is approved in writing.

Test captures may proceed now. The QC lead will record the calibration results and whether the capture preserves the comparison original’s ink-tone distinction. The conservator will make the final color determination, and production scanning dependent on that calibration will begin or resume only after written confirmation of a pass. A lost distinction will require recalibration and a successful retest before production proceeds.

The operator will record checks for completeness, focus, resolution, geometry, color, and the specific ink-tone distinction. The QC lead will review those results, with the conservator confirming color before archive acceptance. Failed tests will be rescanned within the applicable window. Active files will be deleted on the agreed schedule even if testing remains failed or incomplete at expiry, unless a file-specific written extension with a new deadline is already in place. Deletion records will reference the relevant test result or incomplete status, and the established backup-expiry and written-confirmation terms will continue to apply.

We propose Tuesday, 1 December, at 9:00 a.m. local time at the archive, subject to the conservator’s availability. We’ll confirm the appointment once the conservator has agreed to that slot. The amendment terms are settled.

The studio can provisionally hold **Tuesday, 1 December, at 9:00 a.m. local time at the archive**. We will treat the appointment as confirmed only once you notify us that the conservator has accepted the slot. This scheduling hold does not alter the settled amendment terms.
